vulnerability_direction: more negative = larger average rainfall decrease associated with El Nino warming; treated as greater exposure
reason: Uses all 75 years (1950-2024) and is the most stable climate variable (r = 0.98 between RONI and ONI versions); easy unit. Describes a historical association, not a demonstrated cause.

vulnerability_direction: higher = El Nino years more often deficient; treated as greater exposure
reason: Measures how often El Nino years were deficient in this district, using IMD's own category; reasonably stable (r = 0.87 RONI vs ONI). Concern: Pune z = 3.6, partly from suspect IMD years.

vulnerability_direction: higher is treated as greater sensitivity because a larger share of workers is employed in agriculture, which the framework assumes is rainfall-dependent
reason: Directly measures agricultural employment ('agricultural dependency' in the proposal); same formula as the prototype.

vulnerability_direction: higher is treated as greater sensitivity, on the assumption that rainfed crops depend on the monsoon
reason: Irrigation dependence (named in the proposal); chosen over irrigated share so that higher = more vulnerable like most other variables.

vulnerability_direction: higher is treated as greater sensitivity because smaller operational holdings are hypothesised to give less capacity to absorb a failed season
reason: Standard 'small and marginal farmer' definition; no missing values in scope.

vulnerability_direction: higher is used as an adaptive-capacity indicator (treated as lower vulnerability); the framework assumes literacy helps access to information, credit, relief and non-farm work, which this dataset does not test
reason: Only clean adaptive-capacity indicator available; clear direction under the framework; no redundancy.

vulnerability_direction: higher = worse worst-case El Nino monsoon; treated as greater exposure
reason: Worst-case magnitude, stable across indices (r = 0.98); depends on a single year per district, so sensitive to single-year data errors.

vulnerability_direction: higher is treated as greater exposure because more land is under crops that a rainfall deficit can affect
reason: Represents agricultural exposure; overlaps with the climate slope (r = -0.78) because cropland is concentrated in the dry interior.

vulnerability_direction: higher treated as greater sensitivity, on the assumption that seasonal work is less secure
reason: Distinct information (max |r| 0.74 with cropped land); corrected denominator. Skewed (1.6) by tribal districts.

vulnerability_direction: if retained, higher is treated as greater sensitivity as an indirect social-vulnerability indicator; the dataset does not measure household poverty or income
reason: Indirect social-vulnerability indicator (no verified district poverty variable exists in the sources); very skewed (2.4, Nandurbar 69%), so one district can dominate a component.

vulnerability_direction: higher = larger average deficit in El Nino years; treated as greater exposure
reason: Direct and easy to explain, but unstable: r = 0.59 between RONI and ONI versions; Pune is an outlier (z = 2.6) partly because of suspect IMD values.

vulnerability_direction: higher is treated as lower vulnerability, on the assumption that irrigation buffers rainfall deficits
reason: Exact complement of rainfed share; use one. Same information as the chosen rainfed share, opposite sign.

vulnerability_direction: higher treated as greater sensitivity, on the assumption that wage labourers lose work when crops fail
reason: Component of agricultural worker share, but conceptually sharper (landless labour); could replace the total if the guide prefers.

vulnerability_direction: higher is treated as greater sensitivity, on the assumption that rural livelihoods depend more on local rainfall
reason: Overlaps with agricultural worker share (r = 0.87), which measures farm-based work more directly.

vulnerability_direction: if retained, higher is treated as greater sensitivity as an indirect social-vulnerability indicator; the dataset does not measure household poverty or income
reason: Indirect social-vulnerability indicator with no drought mechanism measured here; small spread (3-20%). Option if the guide wants a social-vulnerability dimension.
